the study of a heterogeneous and hierarchical architecture for sensor networks that performs in-network processing and the analysis of its performance and energy consumption.

the design and evaluation of the architecture and the performance of a heterogeneous and hierarchical sensor network.

a heterogeneous hierarchical sensor network outperforms the homogeneous one in terms of energy and time consumption, but the gains depend on the relative density of resource constrained nodes to high-performance ones and the specific node architecture and operation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hierarchical network is a good choice when the energy budget is limited and the accuracy of the output is not a critical requirement for the application.
the use of heterogeneous nodes in sensor networks is a viable option and that the hierarchical organization of these nodes can improve the performance of sensor network applications.
the introduction of hierarchy in a heterogeneous network can improve performance and/or energy consumption for a significant portion of time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of heterogeneous nodes in a network can be used to improve overall performance and reduce energy consumption.

a heterogeneous sensor network that is organized into a hierarchical structure can outperform a homogeneous one even with a low relative density ratio of resource-constrained to high-performance nodes.
the introduction of high-performance nodes in a network of heterogeneous nodes can lead to significant gains in performance and energy consumption.
